pages.text: Approximate hot air output with all inputs supplied:

$(li)$(item)2x2x1$() (4 blocks): about 1 mB per tick$(li)$(item)2x2x2$() (8 blocks): about 5 mB per tick$(li)$(item)2x2x3$() (12 blocks): about 10 mB per tick$(li)$(item)2x2x4$() (16 blocks): about 18 mB per tick$(li)$(item)2x2x5$() (20 blocks): about $(item)28 mB per tick$()$(li)$(item)2x2x6$() (24 blocks): about 40 mB per tick

A blast furnace making steel burns $(item)20 mB of hot air per tick$() while it works. A $(item)2x2x5$() stove covers one furnace with a margin; go higher for two.$(br2)At that size the stove also needs about $(item)28 mB of air$(), $(item)6 mB of fuel$() and gives $(item)28 mB of CO2$() per tick.

The stove pauses when its $(item)hot air$() or $(item)CO2$() tank is full, and when an input tank is empty. A full hot air tank is fine: it means the furnace has all it needs. A full CO2 tank means your exhaust cannot keep up.
